title: Rewrite the question, resize the chunk
brief: Users type three words, or five questions in one breath, or a follow-up that only makes sense with the last turn. The index expects something else. Do you change the query, the chunk grain, or both?

blocks.text: Match the grain of the question to the grain of the chunk

What it does
Helps when

rows: Clean and normalise
Apply to the query the same cleaning you applied to chunks before embedding, for example lowercasing [[r8]]
Always
Skipped cleaning makes query and chunk vectors drift apart
None
Conversation-aware rewrite
Turns a follow-up such as "and for contractors?" into a standalone query using chat history
Multi-turn chat
Pulls stale context into a new topic
1 LLM call
Multi-query
Writes several phrasings and fuses their result lists. Azure offers `queryRewrites: "generative|count-N"`, N from 1 to 10, as a preview feature [[r28]]
Short or vague queries
Near-duplicate lists, extra cost, dropped identifiers
1 LLM call plus N searches
HyDE
An LLM writes a hypothetical answer, and its embedding finds real neighbours [[r14]]
Dense retrieval with no relevance labels, abstract queries
The fake text can contain false details, so only the encoder's filtering protects you
1 LLM call
Step-back
Asks for the higher-level concept or principle first, then reasons from it [[r15]]
Questions tied to specifics that need background principles
Reported gains are on reasoning tasks, not a retrieval benchmark
1 LLM call
Decomposition
Splits a multi-part or multi-hop question into sub-queries that run in parallel
Several parts or hops in one question
Adds a planning call and extra searches to simple lookups, and loses links between parts
1 LLM call plus M searches
Self-query and query hints
Derives metadata filters and boosts from the text. Azure stores hints in `searchIndexParameters.queryHints` [[r29]]
Questions with implied filters such as year or product line
Best effort only, so never use it as an authorization boundary
Planner LLM call

blocks.title: Chunk grain at retrieval time
blocks.intro: You indexed chunks in the previous world. At retrieval time you still choose what you match on and what you hand to the model.

options.name: Small chunks only
options.summary: Match and return the same small passage.
cons: Answers that span a section are cut

options.name: Parent-child (small to big)
options.summary: Match small child chunks, then return the larger parent passage.
cons: Several children can return the same parent, so you must dedupe
Parent and child must inherit the same access rights
options.bestWhen: Questions are precise but answers need the section around the hit.
options.avoidWhen: Parents are huge and the token budget is tight.

options.name: Large chunks only
cons: Embeddings average many topics and blur
options.avoidWhen: Documents mix many topics per section.

options.name: Contextual retrieval
options.summary: Prepend a short LLM-written context to each chunk before embedding and BM25 indexing.
pros: Anthropic reports 35% fewer top-20 retrieval failures with contextual embeddings (5.7% to 3.7%)
49% fewer with contextual BM25 too (to 2.9%), and 67% with reranking added
cons: One LLM call per chunk at index time
The numbers come from the vendor's own datasets
options.bestWhen: Chunks lose meaning when cut out of their document.
options.avoidWhen: You cannot afford re-indexing the corpus.

blocks.title: Rewrites can erase the one token that mattered
blocks.md: Azure's own guidance says rewrites might not contain all the exact terms of the original query, which can hurt highly specific queries that need exact identifiers or product codes [[r28]]. Stored query hints are best effort, are not applied at `minimal` effort, and a GPT-4o or GPT-4.1 family planner returns HTTP 400 at other efforts if stored hints contain a filter [[r29]]. Preview status checked 2026-10-13.

items.symptom: Recall on identifier queries drops after adding an LLM rewrite.
items.cause: The rewrite paraphrased the identifier away.
items.fix: Keep the original query as one fused search, or skip the rewrite when the query has identifier-like tokens. Detect with recall sliced by query class.

items.cause: No conversation-aware rewrite, so the retriever sees three words with no topic.
items.fix: Resolve the follow-up with the chat history before retrieval and log both versions.

items.symptom: Multi-query adds latency and cost but no gain.
items.cause: The variants are near duplicates and return the same top hits.
items.fix: Cap the count, dedupe, and measure uplift per query class before keeping it.

items.symptom: Parent-child fills the prompt with the same section five times.
items.cause: Five child chunks share one parent.
items.fix: Dedupe parents by id before building the prompt.

items.symptom: A generated filter hides the right document.
items.cause: Self-query filters are best effort and can be wrong.
items.fix: Validate against the schema, fall back to unfiltered search on zero hits, and keep access control in a deterministic filter.

quiz.q: Match each query transformation to what it does.

pairs.r: Embeds an LLM-written hypothetical answer to find real neighbours
Asks for the higher-level concept before retrieving
Splits a multi-part question into parallel sub-queries
Turns constraints in the text into metadata filters

quiz.explain: The four transforms answer different problems: a missing relevance signal, missing background, several questions in one, and implied filters. Mixing them up is the common error, for example using HyDE where decomposition is needed.

quiz.q: After adding an LLM query rewrite, recall@10 moved as shown. What is the most likely cause and fix?

code.code:
query class        before  after
identifier         0.91    0.74
paraphrase         0.62    0.71
mixed              0.70    0.73

options: The rewrite drops exact identifiers, so also search with the original query
The embedding model needs to be re-trained on identifier-heavy examples first
The BM25 weight is too high, so lower it for every class
Rewrites should be generated at a higher temperature
quiz.explain: The paraphrase class improved while identifiers dropped, which is the signature of a rewrite that loses exact tokens. Keeping the original query as a fused search restores the identifier hits. Re-training embeddings is a heavy fix for a query-side problem, lowering BM25 would hurt identifiers further, and a higher temperature makes rewrites less faithful.

quiz.q: A user asks: "Compare the notice periods for contractors and employees in the UK and in Germany." Which transformation fits best?
options: HyDE, because the question lacks relevance labels
Step-back, because the question needs a general principle
Decomposition into one sub-query per party and country
Self-query alone, because the countries are filters
quiz.explain: The question has several parts and each needs its own evidence, which is what decomposition and parallel sub-queries provide. HyDE helps one abstract query rather than several parts, step-back targets reasoning that needs a principle, and a country filter alone would still leave contractors and employees in one search.

takeaways: Rewrites help vague queries and follow-ups and can erase exact identifiers
Keep the original query as one of the fused searches
Route by question shape: decompose multi-part questions, leave single lookups alone
Parent-child retrieval needs dedupe of parents and matching access rights
